value.rationale: MNW and leximin are standard competing fairness objectives, while binary additive valuations are a notable domain in which they coincide exactly. Positive \({1,2}\)-valuations are the simplest strictly positive two-level extension, so the first good count at which the two optimizer sets become mutually incompatible is a natural structural boundary. The first layer is especially informative because all conflicts reduce to four symmetry types and the same exact tradeoff between balanced utility \((4,4)\) and higher Nash product at \((3,6)\).
